lines.text: QUESTIONS
1 ) Which concept is illustrated when an employee is granted permission to the company’s new file-
sharing platform for daily use?
A ) Warranty
B ) Goods
C ) Utility
D ) Access to resources
Correct Answer : D
Explanation :
“The service consumer gains access to the service provider’s resources and uses them according to
the agreed terms and conditions.” In this case, the employee is granted permission to use the
‘resource’ of the file sharing platform. Ref 3.1.2
2 ) An IT support engineer assisting a user in configuring their laptop is an example of which
concept?
A ) Transfer of goods
B ) Service actions
C ) Sustainability
D ) Access to resources
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
Service actions are actions “performed by a service provider or jointly by a service provider and a
service consumer. Fulfilment of service requests is a common form of service actions. Other
examples include delivery of goods, user training, consultations, and so on.” In this case, the service
provider team has taken an action by assisting the user. Ref 3.1.2
3 ) What influences whether a service is perceived as valuable by a consumer?
A ) The service provider’s ability to minimize their operational costs
B ) The number of providers delivering the service to the consumer
C ) The extent to which the positive effects of the service outweigh the negative ones
D ) The amount of money the service provider invests in resources
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
Services can introduce new costs and risks, and in some cases, they can negatively affect some of the
intended outcomes, while supporting others. Services are valuable when the positive effects
outweigh the negative ones. Ref 3.1.1
4 ) Which of the following is TRUE regarding services and desired outcomes?
A ) Services guarantee that all intended outcomes will be achieved
B ) Services completely eliminate risks associated with achieving outcomes
C ) Services always result in positive effects without exceptions
D ) Services may have unintended and surprising outcomes, both positive and negative
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
When enabling desired outcomes for service consumers, services may also prevent or reduce other
desired outcomes or introduce undesired ones […] In addition to the intended and anticipated
positive and negative effect on service consumers, services may have unintended and surprising
outcomes, both positive and negative. Ref 3.1.1
QUESTIONS
5 ) A service provider commits to using recyclable components, reducing carbon emissions, and
maintaining transparent supply chains. Which concept does this commitment represent?
A ) Utility
B ) Warranty
C ) User experience
D ) Sustainability
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
“Sustainability requirements may include responsible sourcing of materials and components,
responsible work and employment practices, use of clean energy, low carbon footprint,
incorporation of recycled and recyclable materials, transparent supply chains, and others. These
requirements may originate from national and international regulations and standards or be defined
in the organization’s sustainability strategy.” Ref 3.2.4
6 ) Which dimension of product and service management is directly influenced by leadership
commitment to psychological safety and continual learning?
A ) Partners and suppliers
B ) Value streams and processes
C ) Information and technology
D ) Organizations and people
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
The ‘Organization and people’ dimension is most concerned with establishing a culture of trust.
Digitally enabled organizations are under pressure to continually improve their performance under
changing market conditions […] The challenge for these organizations is to foster an effective set of
shared beliefs, perceptions, and values in relation to risks. This, in turn, should create a safety
culture, and result in behavior that is beneficial for all stakeholders, including the members of the
organization. Ref 2.2.1
7 ) Which of the following dimension of product and service management addresses organizational
and cross-organizational workflows?
A ) Partners and suppliers
B ) Information and technology
C ) Organizations and people
D ) Value streams and processes
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
“The ‘Value streams and processes’ dimension address organizational and cross-organizational
workflows, focusing on what activities the organization undertakes and how they are organized to
enable value for stakeholders effectively and eficiently.” Ref 2.3
8 ) Which dimension of product and service management addresses data and technologies used in
digital product and services?
A ) Partners and suppliers
B ) Organizations and people
C ) Information and technology
D ) Value streams and processes
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
“The ‘Information and technology’ dimension addresses data, information, and technologies used in
QUESTIONS
digital products and services, as well as those used as part of the organization’s product and service
management systems.” Ref 2.4
9 ) Which dimension of product and service management is concerned with relationships with
other organizations that are involved in discovery, design and continual improvement of product?
A ) Value streams and processes
B ) Information and technology
C ) Partners and suppliers
D ) Organizations and people
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
“The ‘Partners and suppliers’ dimension encompasses an organization’s relationships with other
organizations that are involved in the discovery, design, build, transition, operation, delivery, support,
and/or continual improvement of products and services.” Ref 2.5
10 ) According to the ‘Focus on value’ ITIL Guiding Principle, all organizational activities should link
back to what?
A ) Benefits for organization, its customers, and stakeholders
B ) Increased revenue only
C ) Employee satisfaction
D ) Market share dominance
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
The ‘Focus on value’ principle stipulates that all “activities conducted by the organization should link
back, directly or indirectly, to value for itself, its customers, and other stakeholders.” Ref 5.2.1
11 ) According to the ITIL Guiding Principle ‘Start where you are’, what is the MAIN risk of starting
over without considering what is already available when improving a service?
A ) Losing opportunities for collaboration and shared understanding across teams
B ) Overcomplicating solutions by ignoring practical, simple approaches
C ) Failing to gather feedback needed to guide gradual improvement
D ) Wasting time and losing valuable existing capabilities and resources
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
When improving products or services, starting over completely is rarely wise. The approach of
completely removing what has been done “can be extremely wasteful, not only in terms of time, but
also in terms of the loss of existing capabilities, competencies, people, and tools that could have
significant value in the improvement effort. Do not start over without first considering what is
already available to be leveraged.” Ref 5.2.2
12 ) What is the MAIN purpose of using feedback throughout improvement iterations?
A ) To confirm that all stakeholder opinions are in agreement
B ) To ensure that improvement actions remain relevant and effective in changing circumstances
C ) To prevent the need for further adjustments once work has started
D ) To avoid changes in project priorities during implementation
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
Faster response to customer needs is one of the benefits of embedding feedback loops. “Working in
a timeboxed, iterative manner with feedback loops embedded into the workflow allows for […] faster
responses to customer and business needs” Ref 5.2.3.2
QUESTIONS
13 ) A design team is creating a new workflow and tries to account for every possible exception.
What is the consequence of designing the workflow in this way?
A ) Achieving stronger overall risk control
B ) Creating unnecessary complexity
C ) Delivering outcomes more quickly and consistently
D ) Ensuring employees always follow processes without question
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
Trying to provide a solution for every exception will often lead to over-complication. When creating a
product or a practice, designers need to think about exceptions, but they cannot cover them all.
Instead, they should design rules that can be used to handle exceptions generally. Ref 5.2.6
14 ) Why should organizations consider the interaction of ITIL Guiding Principles?
A ) Because principles are interdependent and complement each other
B ) Because one principle is always superior to the rest
C ) Because principles must be applied in a strict order
D ) Because one principle is usually suficient for any situation
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
In addition to being aware of the ITIL Guiding Principles, it is important to recognize that they
interact with and depend upon each other. For example, if an organization is committed to
progressing iteratively with feedback, it should also think and work holistically to ensure that each
iteration of an improvement includes all the elements necessary to deliver real results. Similarly,
making use of appropriate feedback is key to collaboration, and focusing on what will truly be
valuable to the customer makes it easier to keep things simple and practical. Ref 5.2.8
15 ) What is the role of a governing body in an organization?
A ) It is accountable for performance and compliance at the highest level
B ) It is responsible for day-to-day operations
C ) It manages the technical details of digital products directly
D ) It focuses exclusively on financial reporting
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
“Every organization is directed by a governing body: a person or group of people who are
accountable at the highest level for the performance and compliance of the organization.” Ref 5.3.1
16 ) Which of the following is NOT a success metric of ‘discover’ activity?
A ) Strategic fit of the organization’s products and service offerings
B ) Market relevance of the products and service offerings
C ) Service performance against the agreed SLA targets
D ) Stakeholder satisfaction with products and service offerings
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
“Service performance and user feedback records and reports” is part of the ‘Deliver’ activity. The key
metrics of success of the ‘Discover’ activity are: “Strategic fit of the organization’s products and
service offerings; market relevance of the products and service offerings; stakeholder satisfaction
with products and service offerings; commercial success of the products (if applicable).” Ref 4.8.2,
Table 4.7, 4.2.2, Table 4.1
QUESTIONS
17 ) What is a digital service?
A ) A service that fully or largely relies on digital products
B ) A combination of technology resources designed for consumers
C ) The transfer of goods from provider to consumer
D ) A catalogue of services for consumers
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
A digital service is “a service that fully or largely relies on digital products.” Ref 3.1.2
18 ) Which term describes “what an organization does for its consumers and other stakeholders
and why”?
A ) Value stream
B ) Value chain
C ) Operating model
D ) Organization’s purpose
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
An organization’s purpose is “what an organization does for its consumers and other stakeholders
and why.” Ref 5.4.1
19 ) Which statement BEST explains the relationship between an organization’s purpose and its
operating model?
A ) The operating model defines the organization’s financial strategy to achieve its purpose
B ) The organization’s purpose determines why it exists, while the operating model shows how it
fulfils that purpose
C ) The operating model replaces the organization’s purpose once the value chain is defined
D ) The purpose and operating model are unrelated because one focuses on customers and the other
on internal processes
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
An operating model is “A conceptual and/or visual representation of how an organization co-creates
value with its customers and other stakeholders, as well as how the organization runs itself.” Ref
20 ) Which of the following describes a management practice?
A ) A series of steps that an organization uses to create and deliver products
B ) A set of organizational resources and capabilities designed to perform work or accomplish an
objective
C ) A visual representation of how an organization co-creates value with stakeholders
D ) A set of interconnected activities that an organization performs to create and deliver products
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
“Management practice” is “a set of organizational resources and capabilities designed and adopted
for performing work or accomplishing an objective.” Ref 5.5
21 ) Which aspect of an Oficial ITIL Practice Guide describes the roles, competencies, and
responsibilities needed for a specific practice?
A ) Capability assessment and development
B ) General information
QUESTIONS
C ) Organizations and people
D ) Partners and suppliers
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
The Organizations and people aspect of a practice guide describes “roles, competencies and
responsibilities” as well as “organizational solutions and teams (specific to the practice)” Ref 5.5.1,
Table 5.3
22 ) A company plans an improvement initiative and ensures it is clearly linked to organizational
goals and objectives. Which continual improvement step is being performed?
A ) What is the vision?
B ) Where are we now?
C ) Take Action
D ) Where do we want to be?
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
“Each improvement initiative should support the organization’s goals and objectives. The first step of
the continual improvement model is to define the vision of the initiative. This provides context for all
subsequent decisions and links individual actions to the organization’s vision for the future.” Ref
23 ) Which of the following is NOT one of the steps in value stream mapping?
A ) Value stream identification
B ) Mapping of the ‘as-is’ value stream
C ) Mapping a ‘to-be’ value stream
D ) Value stream management
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
Value stream management is not a step in value stream mapping.
Value stream mapping includes the following steps:
1. value stream identification;
2. mapping of the ‘as-is’ value stream;
3. analysing the value stream;
4. mapping a ‘to-be’ value stream;
5. planning and implementing improvements.
Value stream management is used to maintain high quality of services and continually optimize the
flow of work, which means both ‘management of value streams’ and ‘management through value
streams’.
24 ) What is a digital product?
A ) A formal description of one or more services designed to address consumer needs
B ) The access to the service provider’s resources and their use according to the agreed terms and
conditions
C ) A combination of an organization’s resources based on digital technology and designed to offer
value to consumers
D ) Actions performed by a service provider or jointly by a service provider and consumer
Correct answer : C
QUESTIONS
Explanation :
“Digital products are a combination of an organization’s resources based on digital technology and
designed to offer value to consumers.” Ref 4.5.1
25 ) Which of the following is a key success metric for the ‘acquire’ activity?
A ) Number and impact of incidents and performance deviations
B ) Quality of the resources and services outsourced from suppliers
C ) Service performance against the agreed SLA targets
D ) Negative impact of changes on service availability and performance
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
The key metrics of the ‘acquire’ activity are “Quality of the resources and services; acquire cycle
time; adherence to the product roadmap and other relevant guidelines; stakeholder satisfaction with
the ‘acquire’ activity, timelines, and acquired resources.” Ref 4.4.2, Table 4.3
26 ) Which BEST describes the relationship between digital services and digital products?
A ) Digital products are always based on digital services
B ) Digital services are always based on digital products
C ) Digital services and digital products exist independently
D ) Digital products are service actions performed by providers
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
“Digital services are always based on digital products. Products provide capabilities, while service
offerings describe the potential value they offer to customers.” Ref 3.1.2
27 ) Which role takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption?
A ) Organization
B ) Sponsor
C ) Customer
D ) Service provider
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
The “Customer” is the role that defines the requirements for products and services and takes
responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption. Ref 3.2.1.1
28 ) Which type of service relationship typically focuses on support and eficiency through
standardized services?
A ) Basic relationship
B ) Cooperative relationship
C ) Collaborative relationship
D ) Partner relationship
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
The “typical focus” of the ‘basic relationship’ is “support and eficiency”. Ref 3.2.2, Table 3.1
29 ) Which statement about the ‘band of visibility’ is CORRECT?
QUESTIONS
A ) It includes only the activities visible to the service provider
B ) It applies exclusively to modern, technology-based digital service models
C ) It represents all aspects visible between provider and consumer organizations
D ) It defines the complete path of the customer’s service journey
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
The “band of visibility” is the sum of the aspects of the service consumer organizations visible to the
service provider, and the aspects of the service provider organizations visible to the service
consumer. Ref 3.2.3, Figure 3.4
30 ) What is the MAIN purpose of the ‘discover’ activity?
A ) To develop and test digital products
B ) To secure and allocate resources eficiently
C ) To align product capabilities with consumer needs and strategy
D ) To maintain and monitor digital products
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
The main purpose of the ‘discover’ activity “is to ensure continual alignment of the product
roadmaps and related service offerings with the needs of service consumers and with the
organizational strategy.” Ref 4.2.1
31 ) Which lifecycle activity is focused on creating prototypes and specifications?
A ) Design
B ) Deliver
C ) Support
D ) Transition
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
“The purpose of the ‘design’ activity is to create prototypes and specifications for products and
services, detailing their functionality, user experience, and operational framework.” Ref 4.3.1
32 ) What is the PRIMARY purpose of the ‘acquire’ activity?
A ) Resolve incidents and fulfil recovery procedures
B ) Secure and allocate necessary resources eficiently
C ) Provide services and manage user onboarding
D ) Create functional prototypes for testing
Correct answer : B
33 ) Which activity focuses on minimizing the impact of incidents and disasters when they happen?
A ) Transition
B ) Operate
C ) Support
D ) Design
Correct answer : C
QUESTIONS
Explanation :
“The purpose of the ‘support’ activity is to identify and resolve incidents, fulfil disaster recovery
procedures, and capture consumer’s feedback.” Ref 4.9.1
34 ) What does a product specification primarily describe?
A ) Critical aspects, requirements, and characteristics of a product
B ) The initial creation used for testing a product’s design
C ) The ability of a system to remain operational
D ) The process of merging code into a central repository
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
A “product specification” is a detailed document that outlines critical aspects, requirements, and
characteristics of a product or service to be built. It typically includes descriptions of the product or
service features, functionalities, technical requirements, performance criteria, and user interface
details. Ref 4.3.1
35 ) What is an incident in IT services?
A ) Any change of state significant for management
B ) An unplanned interruption to a service or reduction in service quality
C ) A cause of one or more interruptions
D ) A flaw or vulnerability in a service
Correct answer : B
36 ) What BEST describes an event?
A ) A request from a user for a normal service action
B ) A sudden unplanned event causing great damage
C ) Any change of state that has significance for the management of a service
D ) The addition or removal of anything that could have a direct or indirect effect on services
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
An “event” is “any change of state that has significance for the management of a product, service, or
other configuration item.” Ref 4.7.2
37 ) What is continuous integration?
A ) Automatically releasing every code change into production
B ) Regularly merging code into a central repository with automated builds and tests
C ) The ability to track and evaluate service value
D ) A method of ensuring ultra-scalable systems through operations engineering
Correct answer : B
38 ) What BEST describes a Service Level Agreement (SLA)?
A ) A legal contract between two vendors regulating financial penalties
B ) A documented agreement between a service provider and a customer that identifies services and
their agreed levels
C ) An informal discussion between users and service providers about expectations
D ) A guideline document for internal IT teams without customer involvement
QUESTIONS
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
Service Level Agreement (SLA) is “a documented agreement between a service provider and a
customer that identifies the services provided and the agreed level of each service.” Ref 3.2.5
39 ) Which ITIL concept includes governance, practices, and continual improvement?
A ) The ITIL Value System
B ) The “deliver” and “support” value chain activities
C ) The “focus on value” ITIL Guiding Principle
D ) The “value streams and processes” dimension
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
The ITIL Value System (ITIL VS) is a model representing how all the components and activities of an
organization work together to facilitate value creation through digital products and services. Ref 5.1
40 ) What is the MAIN purpose of value stream mapping in an organization?
A ) To automate service monitoring
B ) To identify and prioritize improvement opportunities
C ) To enhance and support management practices
D ) To control external stakeholders directly
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
Value stream mapping “allows organizations to identify, map, and analyse their value streams, as well
as identify and prioritize improvement opportunities.” Ref 6.4
41 ) What is the primary purpose of a product in ITIL digital product and service management?
A ) To offer value to consumers through a defined configuration of resources
B ) To replace service management practices with product management
C ) To enable value co-creation by facilitating outcomes that customers want to achieve
D ) To ensure regulatory compliance across digital services
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
A product is a configuration of an organization’s resources that is designed to offer value. “Digital
product is a combination of an organization’s resources based on digital technology and designed to
offer value to consumers.”
42 ) What is the primary role of a digital service?
A ) To define processes and workflows for value creation
B ) To enable value co-creation by facilitating customer outcomes
C ) To replace product management practices with service management
D ) To ensure compliance with policies and external regulations
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
The core purpose of a service (including a digital service) is to enable value co-creation by helping
consumers achieve desired outcomes, while relieving them of the need to manage certain costs and
risks. “Service is a means of enabling value co-creation by facilitating outcomes that consumers want
to achieve, without the consumer having to manage specific costs and risks.” Ref 3.1.1
QUESTIONS
43 ) Which option is CORRECT in the context of a digital product and a digital service?
A ) A digital service enables value through the use of digital products
B ) A digital product replaces the need for services
C ) A digital service is limited to internal IT systems
D ) A digital service is independent of a digital product
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
In ITIL, a digital service is a service that relies on digital products. Digital products provide the
capabilities, while the digital service uses those capabilities to enable value co-creation for
consumers. “Digital service is a service that fully or largely relies on digital products.” Ref 3.1.2
44 ) A printer is delivered to a customer, while ongoing maintenance and support are provided by
the supplier. Which combination of service interactions is shown in this situation?
A ) Access to resources and service actions
B ) Service offering and service actions
C ) Transfer of goods and service actions
D ) Transfer of goods and service journey
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
The printer being delivered is a transfer of goods, while the ongoing maintenance and support
provided by the supplier represent service actions. ITIL defines these as two distinct forms of service
interaction, and both are present here. “Transfer of goods: some services include transfer of goods
from a service provider to a service consumer.” and “Service action: An action performed by a
service provider or jointly by a service provider and a service consumer.” Ref 3.1.2
45 ) How does ‘access to resources’ support value co-creation in a service interaction?
A ) By allowing consumers to use provider resources
B ) By transferring responsibility for resources to consumers
C ) By limiting resource use to internal teams
D ) By replacing service actions with automation
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
In ITIL, access to resources is a specific form of service interaction where the service consumer uses
the service provider’s resources under agreed conditions. This access enables value co-creation
because consumers can achieve outcomes without owning or managing those resources. “Access to
resources: the service consumer gains access to the service provider’s resources and uses them
according to the agreed terms and conditions.” Ref 3.1.2
46 ) Which of the following is TRUE about value co-creation?
A ) Value is created only by the service provider and delivered to the consumer
B ) Value is defined and consumed by a service provider
C ) Value is created independently of service relationships
D ) Value is created jointly through interactions between service providers and service consumers
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
Value is co-created, it does not exist unless both parties participate. “It is always a combination of
QUESTIONS
service consumption (by the service consumer) and service provision (by the service provider).” Ref
47 ) How do ‘utility’ and ‘warranty’ together support value co-creation?
A ) Utility focuses on cost control, while warranty focuses on risk avoidance
B ) Utility and warranty apply only to products, not services
C ) Utility ensures the service is fit for use, while warranty ensures it is fit for purpose
D ) Utility ensures the service is fit for purpose, while warranty ensures it is fit for use
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
Utility and warranty are two complementary aspects of service value. Utility describes what the
service does (fitness for purpose), while warranty describes how the service performs (fitness for
use). Utility is the functionality offered by a product or service to meet a particular need, and
warranty ensures the service performs and can be used as expected. Ref 3.2.4
48 ) Why does ITIL consider outcomes, costs, and risks together when explaining value co-creation?
A ) Because value is created when desired outcomes are achieved while costs and risks are optimized
B ) Because outcomes eliminate the need to manage costs and risks
C ) Because costs are more important than outcomes
D ) Because risks are more important than outcomes
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
ITIL explains value co-creation as a balance between outcomes, costs, and risks. Value is not created
by outcomes alone; it emerges when desired outcomes are achieved while costs and risks are
appropriately optimized for the service consumer. These three elements must be considered
together to understand whether a service is truly valuable. Ref 3.1.1
49 ) What is service quality most concerned with?
A ) How well a service meets agreed requirements and expectations
B ) How quickly incidents are resolved
C ) The speed of service development
D ) The social responsibility of a service provider
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
Service quality is being concerned with how well a service satisfies stated and implied needs, which
are expressed through agreed requirements and expectations. It is not limited to speed,
development pace, or ethics alone, but to the overall ability of the service to meet what has been
agreed and expected. “Service quality is the sum of the characteristics of a service that are relevant
to its ability to satisfy stated and implied needs.” Ref 3.2.4
50 ) Which of the following is typically used to establish a shared understanding of expected and
achieved service quality?
A ) Product specification
B ) Service level agreement
C ) Product and service roadmaps
D ) Service level requirements
Correct answer : B
QUESTIONS
Explanation :
A Service Level Agreement (SLA) is the common mechanism used to establish a shared
understanding between a service provider and a customer regarding expected and achieved service
quality. It formalizes what level of service is expected and how it will be measured and managed. Ref
51 ) How does the ‘information and technology’ dimension support effective product and service
management?
A ) By enabling the use of data, information, and technology required to deliver services
B ) By defining organizational roles and responsibilities needed for product development
C ) By defining workflows and activities required for product development
D ) By managing relationships with external suppliers
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
The information and technology dimension in ITIL explicitly focuses on the data, information, and
technologies that support digital products and services and the management systems behind them.
This dimension ensures that the right technological capabilities and information assets are available
to enable effective product and service management. Ref 2.4
52 ) Which dimension is concerned with management of relationships with external organizations?
A ) Partners and suppliers
B ) Information and technology
C ) Organizations and people
D ) Value streams and processes
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
The Partners and suppliers dimension explicitly addresses how an organization manages its
relationships with external organizations that contribute to the discovery, design, delivery, support,
and improvement of products and services. Ref 2.5
53) Why are ‘value streams and processes’ important in product and service management?
A ) They specify the tools used for service monitoring
B ) They show how activities are coordinated to create and deliver value
C ) They define organizational hierarchies and reporting lines
D ) They describe supplier agreements and help manage contracts
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
The value streams and processes dimension is concerned with how workflows across activities and
how those activities are organized and coordinated to enable value for stakeholders. “Value stream is
a series of steps that an organization uses to create and deliver products and services to a service
consumer.” Ref 2.3.1
54 ) How does the ‘organizations and people’ dimension contribute to effective product and
service management?
A ) By ensuring skills, culture, and communication support value creation
B ) By defining the technologies used to deliver services
C ) By managing relationships with external organizations
D ) By automating workflows across value streams
QUESTIONS
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
The organizations and people dimension focuses on ensuring that culture, leadership, skills,
competencies, and communication enable the organization to work effectively and create value
through products and services. Ref Glossary
55 ) Which set correctly lists the components of the ITIL Value System (VS)?
A ) Value streams, projects, releases, incidents, changes
B ) Guiding principles, governance, discover, deliver
C ) Products, services, customers, suppliers, partners
D ) Guiding principles, governance, value chain, management practices, continual improvement
Correct answer : D
Explanation :
This includes all five components of the VS. “The ITIL VS includes five components: Guiding
principles, Governance, Value chain, Practices, Continual improvement” Ref 1.3
56 ) A team is developing a new digital service. Instead of delivering all features at once, they
release a small set of features, gather user feedback, and adjust the next release based on what
they learn. Which ITIL Guiding Principle is the team applying in this situation?
A ) Keep it simple and practical
B ) Focus on value
C ) Progress iteratively with feedback
D ) Collaborate and promote visibility
Correct answer : C
Explanation :
The scenario describes releasing work in small increments, gathering feedback, and adjusting future
iterations. “Product and service management iterations can be sequential or simultaneous, with
multiple feedback loops between them.” Ref 5.2.3
57) How should the ITIL Guiding Principle ‘optimize and automate’ be applied?
A ) By replacing people with technology across all functions
B ) By optimizing processes before automating them
C ) By automating all activities immediately
D ) By automating processes before optimizing them
Correct answer : B
Explanation :
Optimization must come before automation. Automating ineficient or poorly designed work only
increases waste and risk. “Before an activity or practice can be effectively automated, it should be
optimized to whatever degree is reasonably possible.” Ref 5.2.7
58 ) What does the ITIL Guiding Principle ‘think and work holistically’ emphasize?
A ) Considering all components of the service value system when making decisions
B ) Assigning responsibility for improvements to a single team
C ) Ensuring all activities result in value creation for the stakeholders
D ) Automating repetitive and manual tasks
Correct answer : A
QUESTIONS
Explanation :
No element of the organization operates in isolation and decisions must consider the whole system,
including interactions across the ITIL Value System. Ref 5.2.5
59 ) How should the ITIL Guiding Principle ‘collaborate and promote visibility’ be applied?
A ) By involving stakeholders and sharing information with them
B ) By limiting communication to management only
C ) By reusing existing processes wherever possible
D ) By capturing feedback after each iteration
Correct answer : A
Explanation :
Collaborate and promote visibility explicitly emphasizes working with stakeholders and making work
and information visible to enable better decision-making, trust, and outcomes. “When initiatives
involve the right people in the correct roles, efforts benefit from better buy-in, more relevance
(because better information is available for decision-making) and increased likelihood of long-term
success.” Ref 5.2.4
60 ) How does ITIL describe the way the Guiding Principles should be applied together?
A ) They should be applied one at a time in a fixed sequence
B ) They replace the need for governance and management practices
C ) They should be applied independent of each other
D ) They should be used collectively and balanced based on the situation
Correct answer : D
Explanation :

207. What is the outcome of the Service Value System?
A) A new software version
B) An incident report
C) Value
D) A service request
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
The ultimate goal and result of the entire value system is the creation of value.
208. Which component of the VS is defined as "The system by which an organization is directed
and controlled"?
A) Management practices
B) Governance
C) Continual improvement
D) Value chain
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Governance provides the oversight and direction for the organization.
209. What are "Management Practices" in the VS?
A) The final outputs of the system.
B) Universal ethical guidelines.
C) Sets of organizational capabilities for accomplishing specific objectives
D) The steps in a software development lifecycle.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Practices are specialized capabilities, such as Incident Management or Service Desk, used to
perform work.
210. What is the "Value Chain" within the VS?
A) A hierarchy of senior managers.
B) Interconnected activities that create and deliver products and services
C) A list of external suppliers.
D) A database of customer complaints.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
The value chain represents the internal activities (like Design, Build, Deliver) that transform
demand into value.
211. The ITIL VS is described as a "series of steps". What do these steps ultimately produce?
A) Technology resources
B) Project plans
C) Only internal documentation
D) Products and services delivered to a consumer
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
The system is designed to create and deliver the actual products and services that provide value.
212. What is continual improvement?
A) One-time project
B) Recurring activity to improve services and practices
C) Governance policy
D) Service lifecycle stage
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
In ITIL, continual improvement is an ongoing, iterative process aimed at enhancing services,
practices, and all elements of the service value system. It is not a one-time effort, nor just a
governance policy or a specific lifecycle stage—it happens continuously across the organization.
213. Which statement about the ITIL Value System (VS) is CORRECT?
A) It is a rigid, linear sequence of steps used only by external vendors.
B) Each organization's VS interfaces with others to form a value-facilitating ecosystem.
C) It is designed to replace the need for management practices.
D) The VS has no inputs and only focuses on internal outputs.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Every organization's Value System (VS) interacts with those of other organizations, creating an
ecosystem that facilitates value co-creation for all stakeholders.
214. Which governance activity is focused on ensuring adherence with policies and strategic
direction?
A) Evaluate
B) Direct
C) Monitor
D) Discover
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
“Monitor” is the activity explicitly concerned with checking that performance and activities adhere
to policies and strategic direction.
“Monitor: monitoring the performance of the organization and its practices, products, and services.
The governing body ensures that performance is in accordance with policies and strategic
direction.” Ref 5.3.1
215. What is the role of a governing body in an organization?
A) It is accountable for performance and compliance at the highest level
B) It is responsible for day-to-day operations
C) It manages the technical details of digital products directly
D) It focuses exclusively on financial reporting
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
Every organization is directed by a governing body: —a person or group of people who are
accountable at the highest level for the performance and compliance of the organization.
216. What is the primary role of the "Governing Body"?
A) To write the software code.
B) To handle daily support calls.
C) Accountability at the highest level for organizational performance and compliance
D) To manage external marketing campaigns.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
The governing body (like a Board of Directors) is responsible for the overall direction and legality
of the organization.
217. Which activity of governance involves establishing and modifying policies and strategies?
A) Evaluate
B) Direct
C) Monitor
D) Support
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
"Directing" is the act of setting goals, strategy, and the rules (policies) the organization must
follow.
218. What does the "Monitor" activity in governance focus on?
A) Performance and compliance with policies and regulations
B) Brainstorming new product ideas.
C) Hiring new junior employees.
D) Repairing broken hardware.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
Once direction is set, the governing body must oversee if those rules are being followed and goals
are being met.
219. Governance of digital technology is a part of which broader system?
A) Project management
B) Software development
C) Corporate governance
D) Incident management
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Managing how technology is used is a critical component of overall corporate oversight.
220. Why does the governing body "Evaluate" the organization?
A) To find reasons to fire employees.
B) To assess the current state, strategies, and portfolios to identify needs
C) To check the battery life of laptops.
D) To write user manuals for new apps.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Evaluation is necessary to understand if the current strategy is effective and what changes are
needed.
221. Who typically makes up a governing body?
A) Only junior software developers.
B) A board of directors or executive managers
C) External customers only.
D) Only the IT service desk team.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
High-level executives or a board typically take on the governance role.
222. Which governance activity involves engaging stakeholders to clarify commitments?
A) Direct
B) Monitor
C) Engage stakeholders
D) Build
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
The governing body must talk to stakeholders to identify needs and agree on accountability.
223. The goal of digital technology governance is ensuring technology use is:
A) As expensive as possible.
B) Unregulated and free-form.
C) Responsible, ethical, and aligned with organizational goals
D) Only used for internal social media.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Governance ensures that tech investments actually drive the business goals in a legal and ethical
way.
224. which governance activity involves assessment of an organization's current strategies,
portfolios, and relationships?
A) Direct
B) Monitor
C) Evaluate
D) Engage stakeholders
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
The governance activity of "Evaluate" is where the governing body assesses the current state of the
organization, including its strategies, portfolios, and policies.
225. What is the primary purpose of the "Monitor" activity within the governance of digital
technology?
A) To identify new technology needs through stakeholder engagement.
B) To oversee performance and compliance once policies and strategies are in place.
C) To establish and modify organizational policies.
D) To define the current state of organizational relationships.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
The "Monitor" activity is specifically described as oversight by the governing body to check
performance and compliance after policies and strategies have been established.
226. According to the ‘Focus on value’ ITIL Guiding Principle, all organizational activities should
link back to what?
A) Benefits for organization, its customers, and stakeholders
B) Increased revenue only
C) Employee satisfaction
D) Market share dominance
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
The ‘Focus on value’ guiding principle stipulates that “all activities conducted by the organization
should link back, directly or indirectly, to value for itself, its customers, and other stakeholders.”
227. According to the ITIL Guiding Principle ‘Start where you are’, what is the MAIN risk of
starting over without considering what is already available when improving a service?
A) Losing opportunities for collaboration and shared understanding across teams
B) Overcomplicating solutions by ignoring practical, simple approaches
C) Failing to gather feedback needed to guide gradual improvement
D) Wasting time and losing valuable existing capabilities and resources
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
When improving products or services, starting over completely is rarely wise. The approach of
completely removing what has been done “can be extremely wasteful, not only in terms of time, but
also in terms of the loss of existing capabilities, competencies, people, and tools that could have
significant value in the improvement effort. Do not start over without first considering what is
already available to be leveraged.” Ref 5.2.2
228. Why should organizations consider the interaction of ITIL Guiding Principles?
A) Because principles are interdependent and complement each other
B) Because one principle is always superior to the rest
C) Because principles must be applied in a strict order
D) Because one principle is usually sufficient for any situation
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
“In addition to being aware of the ITIL guiding principles, it is important to recognize that they
interact with and depend upon each other. For example, if an organization is committed to
progressing iteratively with feedback, it should also think and work holistically to ensure that each
iteration of an improvement includes all the elements necessary to deliver real results. Similarly,
making use of appropriate feedback is key to collaboration, and focusing on what will truly be
valuable to the customer makes it easier to keep things simple and practical.” Ref 5.2.8
229. Which principle recommends assessing what is already available before starting a new
initiative?
A) Focus on value
B) Start where you are
C) Optimize and automate
D) Think and work holistically
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
This principle warns against "ripping and replacing" when existing resources can be leveraged.
230. Which principle focuses on the idea that "no product, service, or team stands alone"?
A) Keep it simple and practical
B) Focus on value
C) Progress iteratively with feedback
D) Think and work holistically
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
This principle emphasizes understanding the integrated nature of all organizational parts.
231. What does the "Focus on Value" principle require as a first step?
A) Buying the most expensive tools.
B) Knowing who is being served (the service consumer)
C) Writing a 100-page project plan.
D) Automating all manual tasks.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
You cannot provide value if you don't know who the consumer is and what they need.
232. What is the core recommendation of "Optimize and Automate"?
A) Automate every manual task immediately.
B) Simplify and optimize a process before attempting to automate it
C) Only use automation if it increases the number of staff needed.
D) Avoid using AI at all costs.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
In ITIL (Guiding Principle: Optimize and Automate), the key recommendation is:
• First analyze and improve (optimize) the process.
• Then automate only what is efficient and valuable.
Automating a broken or inefficient process will only make problems happen faster and at scale.
233. Which statement about the Guiding Principles is CORRECT?
A) They must be followed in a specific numerical order.
B) "Focus on Value" is more important than all others.
C) They interact with and depend on each other
D) They only apply to technical staff.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Principles should be considered together as they complement each other in different situations.
234. Under "Start where you are", why is direct observation important?
A) To make employees feel nervous.
B) Because there is often a discrepancy between reports and reality
C) To avoid having to use any data or metrics.
D) To check if employees are wearing their uniforms.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Reports can be biased or distorted; seeing the work directly provides accurate information for
decisions.
235. "Progress iteratively with feedback" allows organizations to:
A) Finish a three-year project before showing it to the customer.
B) Ignore all customer opinions until the very end.
C) Detect and respond to failures earlier
D) Ensure that the project plan never changes.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Working in small chunks with feedback loops makes the organization more flexible and higher
quality.
236. Which statement BEST describes a recommendation of the "Keep it simple and practical"
principle?
A) Design a unique solution for every possible exception to ensure complete coverage.
B) If a process, product, or metric fails to increase value or produce a useful outcome, eliminate it.
C) Prioritize complex technical features over outcome-based thinking to ensure sophistication.
D) Focus only on the needs of technical staff when designing rules to handle exceptions.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
The "Keep it simple and practical" principle emphasizes outcome-based thinking. If a component
(process, product, service, action, or metric) does not contribute to value or a useful outcome, it
should be eliminated rather than maintained. It also warns that trying to provide a solution for every
exception leads to over-complication.
237. What is the MAIN purpose of the "discover" activity?
A) To develop and test digital products
B) To secure and allocate resources efficiently
C) To align product capabilities with consumer needs and strategy
D) To maintain and monitor digital products
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
The main purpose of the "discover" activity "is to ensure continual alignment of the product
roadmaps and related service offerings with the needs of service consumers and with the
organizational strategy."
238. Which of the following is NOT a success metric of ‘Discover’ activity?
A) Strategic fit of the organization’s products and service offerings
B) Market relevance of the products and service offerings
C) Service performance against the agreed SLA targets
D) Stakeholder satisfaction with products and service offerings
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
“Service performance and user feedback records and reports” is part of the ‘Deliver’ activity. The
key metrics of success of the ‘Discover’ activity are: Strategic fit of the organization’s products and
service offerings; market relevance of the products and service offerings; stakeholder satisfaction
with products and service offerings; commercial success of the products (if applicable).
Ref 4.8.2, Table 4.7, 4.2.2, Table 4.1
239. Which activity focuses on minimizing the impact of incidents and disasters when they happen?
A) Transition
B) Operate
C) Support
D) Design
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
"The purpose of the ‘support’ activity is to identify and resolve incidents, fulfill disaster recovery
procedures, and capture consumer’s feedback." Ref 4.9.1
240. What is an "Operating Model"?
A) A physical prototype of a machine.
B) A visual representation of how an organization co-creates value and runs itself
C) A list of all software licenses owned by the company.
D) The legal document that incorporates a business.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
It shows the "big picture" of how people, processes, and technology work together to deliver value.
241. What is a "Product Prototype"?
A) A finished product ready for mass market.
B) A technical manual for an old system.
C) An initial version used to test design, functionality, and hypotheses
D) A legal contract with a supplier.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Prototypes are used during the "Design" activity to refine ideas before full building starts.
242. Which activity transforms solution designs into functional digital products?
A) Acquire
B) Build
C) Transition
D) Operate
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
"Build" is the development and integration phase of the lifecycle.
243. Which value chain activity moves built products into the live environment?
A) Design
B) Acquire
C) Transition
D) Support
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Transition ensures products are ready for operation and service delivery.
244. What is an "Incident"?
A) A planned maintenance window.
B) A user asking for a new password.
C) An unplanned interruption to or reduction in the quality of a service
D) A change in the company's CEO.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Incidents are failures that need to be resolved by the "Support" activity.
245. Which activity focuses on fulfilling service requests and managing user onboarding?
A) Discover
B) Build
C) Deliver
D) Transition
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
"Deliver" is the user-facing activity that ensures services are provided according to SLAs.
246. What is "Observability" in the context of the "Operate" activity?
A) Watching employees to make sure they are working.
B) Understanding a system's internal state by analyzing external outputs (logs, traces)
C) Reading the newspaper to see what competitors are doing.
D) Checking the physical temperature of the server room.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
It allows operations teams to understand complex systems without needing to take them apart.
247. What is a "Problem" in ITIL?
A) A cause, or potential cause, of one or more incidents
B) A customer who refuses to pay their bill.
C) A software update that adds new features.
D) A project that is behind schedule.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
Support teams investigate incidents to find the underlying "problem" (cause) to prevent future
failures.
248. What is the definition of a "Known Error" in ITIL?
A) A flaw or vulnerability that may cause incidents
B) A problem that has been analysed but has not been resolved
C) A sudden unplanned event that causes serious loss to an organization
D) The cause, or potential cause, of one or more incidents.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
A Known Error is specifically defined as a problem that has undergone analysis but remains
unresolved. This distinguishes it from a generic Problem (the cause of incidents) or an Error (a flaw
that may cause incidents).
249. Which term describes ‘what an organization does for its consumers and other stakeholders and
why’?
A) Value stream
B) Value chain
C) Operating model
D) Organization’s purpose
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
Option A is incorrect. ‘Value stream’ is a term for “a series of steps that an organization uses to
create and deliver products and services to a service consumer.” Ref 6.1
Option B is incorrect. The ‘Value chain’ enables and supports the value streams, in addition,
“continual improvement of value streams is achieved indirectly by improving the value chain and
the management practices.” Ref 6.4
Option C is incorrect. The operating model is a “conceptual and/or visual representation of how an
organization co-creates value with its customers and other stakeholders, as well as how the
organization runs itself.” Ref Glossary
Option D is correct. An organization’s purpose is “what an organization does for its consumers and
other stakeholders and why.” Ref 5.4.1
250. Which of the following is NOT one of the steps in value stream mapping?
A) Value stream identification
B) Mapping of the ‘as-is’ value stream
C) Mapping a ‘to-be’ value stream
D) Value stream management
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
“Value stream mapping includes the following steps: value stream identification; mapping of the
‘as-is’ value stream; analysing the value stream; mapping a ‘to-be’ value stream; planning and
implementing improvements.” Ref 6.3, Glossary
251. What is the MAIN purpose of value stream mapping in an organization?
A) To automate service monitoring
B) To identify and prioritize improvement opportunities
C) To enhance and support management practices
D) To control external stakeholders directly
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Value stream mapping "allows organizations to identify, map, and analyse their value streams, as
well as identify and prioritize improvement opportunities." Ref 6.4
252. What is a "Value Stream"?
A) A fast-moving river used for power generation.
B) A series of steps an organization uses to create and deliver products/services
C) A list of high-value customers.
D) The total revenue generated in one month.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
It represents the actual end-to-end workflow used to deliver value.
253. What is the purpose of "Value Stream Mapping"?
A) To visualize and analyze the flow of work and information to improve quality
B) To create a map of the office building.
C) To track the GPS location of delivery trucks.
D) To draw a diagram of the computer network.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
Mapping helps clarify how value is created and identifies waste in the process.
254. Which of these is a "Core Value Stream"?
A) A process for internal employee payroll.
B) A stream that enables value for consumers as intended by the operating model
C) The procedure for cleaning the office.
D) A training program for internal staff.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Core streams are the ones directly delivering the organization's primary products/services to
external customers.
255. What is an "Enabling Value Stream"?
A) A stream that generates the most profit.
B) A stream that is only used once a year.
C) A stream that requires no technology.
D) A stream that enables value for internal customers to support core streams
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
These are supporting workflows, like internal IT support, that allow the core business to function.
256. In value stream mapping, what is "as-is" mapping?
A) Designing a perfect future process.
B) Documenting the current state of the workflow as it actually exists
C) Guessing how the process worked ten years ago.
D) Writing a marketing brochure for the process.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
You must understand the current reality before you can plan improvements.
257. What is "Value Stream Management"?
A) A one-time exercise to draw a diagram.
B) A software tool for managing bank accounts.
C) An ongoing focus on analyzing and improving how work is done
D) Hiring a consultant to manage all employees.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
While mapping is a technique, management is the continuous practice of optimizing those streams.
258. What is "waste" in a value stream?
A) Physical trash in the office.
B) Money spent on marketing.
C) Customers who don't buy anything.
D) Non-value-adding activities
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
In a value stream, waste refers to:
Any activity that does not add value to the customer
Things that consume time, effort, or resources without improving the outcome
Examples include delays, rework, unnecessary approvals, and excessive handoffs.
259. What is the final step in the value stream mapping process?
A) Identify the stream.
B) Map the "as-is" stream.
C) Plan and implement improvements
D) Analyze the stream.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Value stream mapping is a technique used to visualize and analyze the flow of work and
information. The process follows a structured sequence of five steps:
1. Identify the value stream: Determine which stream needs to be analyzed.
2. Map the ‘as-is’ stream: Document the current state of the workflow as it exists.
3. Analyse the stream: Look for waste (non-value-adding activities) and opportunities for
optimization.
4. Map the ‘to-be’ stream: Design the desired future state of the workflow.
5. Plan and implement improvements: This is the final step, where the organization actually
executes changes to achieve the target state.
260. How does automation support value stream management?
A) By replacing all human managers.
B) By ensuring the process never has to be mapped.
C) By providing measurement and data to analyze performance
D) By automatically firing employees who are slow.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Automation can provide real-time metrics that help managers see where a stream is failing or
succeeding.
261. A company plans an improvement initiative and ensures it is clearly linked to organizational
goals and objectives. Which continual improvement step is being performed?
A) What is the vision?
B) Where are we now?
C) Take Action
D) Where do we want to be?
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
“Each improvement initiative should support the organization’s goals and objectives. The first step
of the continual improvement model is to define the vision of the initiative. This provides context
for all subsequent decisions and links individual actions to the organization’s vision for the future.”
262. In the "Where are we now?" step, what should be assessed?
A) Existing products, services, processes, and culture
B) Only the salaries of the IT team.
C) The color of the office walls.
D) The CEO's personal social media account.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
You must have a clear baseline of the current state before you can measure progress.
263. What is the goal of the "Where do we want to be?" step?
A) To complain about the current situation.
B) To define the desired future state with measurable objectives (KPIs)
C) To pick a random date for a party.
D) To buy a new software tool without a plan.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
This step defines "Point B" so the organization knows exactly what success looks like.
264. What does "How do we get there?" involve?
A) Waiting for someone else to fix the problem.
B) Planning the route and identifying iterations or experiments
C) Spending the entire budget on a single day.
D) Only doing work if it can be finished in one day.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
This is the planning phase where expertise is used to map out the improvement journey.
265. Which statement about the "Take action" step is CORRECT?
A) Plans must never be changed once they start.
B) Results should only be measured at the very end.
C) Action should only be taken by senior managers.
D) Work should be done iteratively, adapting and changing direction if needed
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
Improvement work is often complex and requires constant adjustment based on reality.
266. What happens in the "Are we getting there?" step?
A) Assessing progress against objectives and value
B) Starting a completely new and unrelated project.
C) Forgetting about the vision and doing something else.
D) Only celebrating even if results were bad.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
This is the validation step to see if the actions taken actually moved the organization closer to the
vision.
267. How do organizations "keep the improvements relevant"?
A) By firing the people who worked on the improvement.
B) By using change and knowledge management to embed the new ways of working
C) By immediately going back to the old way of doing things.
D) By keeping the success a secret from other teams.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
"How do we keep the improvements relevant?"
When targets are met:
• Use change and knowledge management to embed improvements.
• Leaders/managers help teams adopt new ways of working.
When targets are not met:
• Inform stakeholders of reasons for failure.
• Analyse, document, and share lessons learned.
• Suggest improvements for next iteration.
• Treat deviations as learning opportunities, not blame.
268. Which step of the Continual Improvement Model focuses on the organization's vision?
A) What is the vision?
B) Where are we now?
C) How do we get there?
D) Take action
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
This first step ensures that any improvement initiative is aligned with the high-level goals of the
business.
269. If an improvement target is NOT met, what should the organization do?
A) Blame and punish the employees involved.
B) Hide the failure from stakeholders.
C) Never try to improve anything ever again.
D) Analyze and share lessons learned as an opportunity for the next iteration
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
"How do we keep the improvements relevant?"
When targets are met:
• Use change and knowledge management to embed improvements.
• Leaders/managers help teams adopt new ways of working.
When targets are not met:
• Inform stakeholders of reasons for failure.
• Analyse, document, and share lessons learned.
• Suggest improvements for next iteration.
• Treat deviations as learning opportunities, not blame.
270. Continual improvement applies to which parts of the ITIL Value System?
A) Only the software code
B) Only the external suppliers
C) Everything: products, services, practices, and relationships
D) Only the help desk
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
No part of the organization is exempt from the need to get better over time.
271. Which step of the ITIL continual improvement model involves defining the desired future state
using measurable objectives and progress criteria?
A) What is the vision?
B) Where are we now?
C) Where do we want to be?
D) How do we get there?
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
The "Where do we want to be?" step is focused on defining the desired future state (Point B) by
setting clear improvement objectives with Critical Success Factors (CSFs) and Key Performance
Indicators (KPIs).
272. What should an organization do if an improvement initiative reaches the "Are we getting
there?" step and finds that results have fallen short of the objectives?
A) Immediately ignore the vision and start an unrelated project.
B) Plan additional actions or start a new iteration.
C) Punish the teams involved in the deviation.
D) Hide the results from stakeholders to maintain momentum.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
During the "Are we getting there?" step, if results fall short of the established objectives, the
organization should plan additional actions or a new iteration to address the gap.
273. Which dimension of product and service management is directly influenced by leadership
commitment to psychological safety and continual learning?
A) Partners and suppliers
B) Value streams and processes
C) Information and technology
D) Organizations and people
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
The ‘Organization and people’ dimension is most concerned with establishing a culture of trust.
“Digitally enabled organizations are under pressure to continually improve their performance under
changing market conditions. [...]. The challenge for these organizations is to foster an effective set
of shared beliefs, perceptions, and values in relation to risks. This, in turn, should create a safety
culture, and result in behaviour that is beneficial for all stakeholders, including the members of the
organization.” Ref 2.2.1
274. Which of the following dimension of product and service management addresses
organizational and cross-organizational workflows?
A) Partners and suppliers
B) Information and technology
C) Value streams and processes
D) Organizations and people
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
“The ‘Value streams and processes’ dimension address organizational and cross-organizational
workflows, focusing on what activities the organization undertakes and how they are organized to
enable value for stakeholders effectively and efficiently.” Ref 2.3
275. Which dimension of product and service management addresses data and technologies used in
digital product and services?
A) Organizations and people
B) Partners and suppliers
C) Information and technology
D) Value streams and processes
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
“The ‘Information and technology’ dimension addresses data, information, and technologies used
in digital products and services, as well as those used as part of the organization’s product and
service management systems.” Ref 2.4
276. What is the purpose of the "Four Dimensions"?
A) To support a holistic approach to service management
B) To divide the IT department into four separate buildings.
C) To create four different versions of every software product.
D) To ensure every project has exactly four managers.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
Focusing on all four dimensions ensures that no critical aspect (like people or suppliers) is ignored.
277. What is "Organizational Culture"?
A) The dress code of the company.
B) The physical location of the headquarters.
C) A set of shared values, beliefs, and practices expressed through behavior
D) The total number of employees.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Culture is "how we do things around here" and is shaped by values and leadership.
278. Which dimension covers data, analytics, and cloud computing?
A) Organizations and People
B) Information and Technology
C) Partners and Suppliers
D) Value Streams and Processes
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
This dimension focuses on the tools and information used to create value.
279. What is "Conway's Law"?
A) A law about the speed of computer processors.
B) The idea that system designs mirror the communication structure of the organization
C) A regulation about data privacy in Europe.
D) A rule stating that every team must have an AI assistant.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Conway’s Law: Systems mirror the communication structure of the organizations that build them.
280. What does "Data Governance" ensure?
A) That data remains secure, usable, and reliable throughout its lifecycle
B) That all data is deleted after 24 hours.
C) That only the CEO can see the company's data.
D) That data is stored on physical paper only.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
Data governance: A system of rules, policies, standards, processes, and controls organizations
implement to manage their data assets effectively.
281. Which dimension deals with third-party relationships and contracts?
A) Organizations and People
B) Information and Technology
C) Partners and Suppliers
D) Value Streams and Processes
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
The Partners and Suppliers dimension in ITIL focuses on:
Third-party relationships
Suppliers and vendors
Contracts and agreements
It ensures that external parties effectively support service delivery and value creation.
282. Which factor might influence an organization's "Supplier Strategy"?
A) Resource scarcity, cost concerns, and corporate culture
B) The personal hobbies of the junior staff.
C) The color of the supplier's logo.
D) The type of coffee served in the cafeteria.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
The supplier strategy is shaped by practical concerns like budget, expertise, and external
regulations.
283. The "Value Streams and Processes" dimension focuses on:
A) Buying new computers.
B) What activities the organization undertakes and how they are organized
C) Hiring more people to do the same work.
D) Writing more internal emails.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
The ‘value streams and processes’ dimension addresses organizational and cross-organizational
workflows, focusing on what activities the organization undertakes and how they are organized to
enable value for stakeholders effectively and efficiently.
284. Which dimension addresses culture, competencies, and leadership?
A) Organizations and People
B) Information and Technology
C) Partners and Suppliers
D) Value Streams and Processes
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
(Organizations and People) dimension focuses on the human side of service management.
285. How does ITIL collaborate with DevOps practices to support digital product and service

A) By providing the framework while DevOps supplies practices and techniques

D) By positioning DevOps as a governance framework over ITIL
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
“DevOps is a valuable complementary approach which should be used as a source of detailed
practical advice enabling such activities of the ITIL Product and Service Lifecycle” explaining that

286. Why is project management important within the ITIL framework?

B) It replaces product and service management practices
C) It supports the implementation and transformation of products and services

Explanation:
“PRINCE2 equips professionals with the tools to manage projects that implement or transform
those products and services” explains the importance of project management for delivery and
change. Ref 7.3.2
D. Incorrect. “Service level management” is a distinct ITIL practice, not the purpose of project

287. How can ITIL and PRINCE2 Agile be used together to deliver products and services?
A) ITIL replaces PRINCE2 governance structures
B) PRINCE2 Agile defines service management practices
C) ITIL manages projects while PRINCE2 Agile manages the daily and overall delivery of services
D) ITIL provides service management guidance while PRINCE2 Agile manages project delivery

Explanation:
“While ITIL focuses on the digital product and services management, PRINCE2 equips

288. What is "DevOps"?
A) A specific type of computer hardware.
B) Practical techniques for rapid, continuous delivery and operational practices
C) A set of laws governing international trade.
D) A replacement for the ITIL framework.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
DevOps provides the "how-to" for fast, agile development and stable operations.
289. What is "PRINCE2"?
A) A new programming language.
B) A type of cloud storage service.
C) A comprehensive method for project, programme, and portfolio management
D) A governing body for international sports.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
PRINCE2 is a widely used framework specifically for managing projects.
290. Integrating ITIL and PRINCE2 ensures alignment between:
A) Marketing and Sales only.
B) Strategy, change initiatives, and operations
C) The office building and the parking lot.
D) Junior staff and their families.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Integrating ITIL and PRINCE2 creates a smooth flow from high-level vision to project delivery to
daily support.
291. Which framework offers "agile, continuous development" practices?
A) PRINCE2
B) Governance
C) DevOps
D) The 6C Model
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
DevOps is synonymous with agile methodologies in a technology context.
292. PRINCE2 supports the "transition" of project outputs into:
A) Physical trash.
B) Managed, valuable services
C) Another project that never ends.
D) A technical manual that no one reads.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
In PRINCE2, the purpose of a project is to deliver outputs that are transitioned into outcomes and
benefits.
293. Large or complex initiatives often require comprehensive methods like:
A) Checking a single box on a list.
B) Sending a single email to all staff.
C) PRINCE2 Project Management
D) Guessing what to do next.
Correct answer: C
Explanation:
Complexity requires a structured approach to manage risks, budgets, and timelines.
294. How does DevOps enhance "execution" in the value chain?
A) Through automation, collaboration, and fast feedback
B) By making every task manual.
C) By preventing teams from talking to each other.
D) By avoiding the use of metrics.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
DevOps principles match perfectly with ITIL guiding principles like "Collaborate" and "Progress
Iteratively".
295. The ultimate goal of integrating ITIL, DevOps, and PRINCE2 is to deliver:
A) The most expensive services possible.
B) Resilient, adaptive, and customer-focused services
C) A collection of documents that are never used.
D) Services that never change for 50 years.
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
Framework integration allows organizations to be agile enough to change while remaining stable
enough to trust.
296. How do ITIL and DevOps work together?
A) ITIL provides structure and governance; DevOps enables rapid development
B) They are competitors and cannot be used at the same time.
C) DevOps is used for small companies; ITIL is only for large ones.
D) ITIL replaces the need for any technical operational practices.
Correct answer: A
Explanation:
Together, they balance the need for stability (ITIL) with the need for speed (DevOps).
297. Which BEST explains why an organization might choose to utilize external suppliers?
A) To maintain greater control and visibility over service delivery
B) To minimize reliance on third-party providers
C) To remove the need for oversight, governance, and internal management
D) To obtain capabilities that are difficult to develop internally
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
Organizations may utilize external suppliers due to resource scarcity, which includes a lack of
needed skills or resources internally. It also allows them to leverage the subject matter expertise and
knowledge of the supplier.
298. Why is project management important in ITIL?
A) To manage routine operational activities and service requests
B) To define governance authority across the ITIL Value System
C) To deliver time-bound initiatives that introduce new or changed services
D) To enable structured delivery of change while services continue to operate
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
Project management is essential for delivering change within the ITIL Value System. Effective projects
ensure that delivery is structured, controlled, and strategically aligned. PRINCE2 methods specifically
support the delivery of changes that implement or modify products and services.
299. A telecom provider designs an enterprise package that contains internet, VoIP, network
security, and technical support. Which concept does this illustrate?
A) Transfer of goods
B) Service action
C) Access to resources
D) Service offering
Correct answer: D
Explanation:
A service offering is a formal description of one or more services designed to address the needs of a
target consumer group, and it can include goods, access to resources, and service actions.
301. What is the purpose of the ITIL AI Capability Model?
A) To describe how service providers, service consumers, and other parties interact with AI to co-
create value
B) To describe how organizations can assess and develop capabilities for effective use of AI
C) To prescribe specific AI technologies required for service development and management
D) To measure the performance of AI-enabled services against predefined service levels
Correct answer: B
Explanation:
The ITIL AI Capability Model helps outline AI's functional capabilities (like the 6C model) and
connects them with assessing existing capabilities to address any gaps with clear action plans.
302. Which value chain activity is addressed by evaluating the quality of the resources and services
sourced from a third party?
A) Build
B) Design
C) Acquire
D) Discover

Explanation:
The "acquire" activity has specific success metrics, one of which is the quality of resources and
services obtained.
